findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata has no `sender` (500 during install)
findings.body: `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` compares the pipeline-stored GitHub login against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` with direct subscripting. `sender` is only ever written by `GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration` when the incoming state carries it (`if state.get("sender")`), i.e. only for Integrations created from the GitHub `installation` webhook. Integrations created through the install pipeline itself have no `sender` key (see `test_basic_flow`, which asserts metadata without `sender`), and all Integration rows that pre-date the webhook handler also lack it. Any time this branch is reached for such a row (Integration exists, no OrganizationIntegration — e.g. a re-install after the org integration was removed, or a self-hosted instance where webhooks are not delivered), the view raises `KeyError` and the user gets an unhandled 500 instead of the intended error page. Use `.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and decide explicitly how to behave when it is absent.

findings.title: Identity check uses mutable GitHub login instead of immutable user id
findings.body: The new authenticity check compares the OAuth-authenticated GitHub `login` string to the `login` stored in `integration.metadata["sender"]` at webhook time. GitHub usernames are renameable and, once freed, re-registerable by anyone. Consequences: (a) a legitimate installer who renames their GitHub account is permanently locked out of re-installing (generic "Invalid installation request."), and (b) an attacker who registers the installer's abandoned username passes the check. The webhook stores the sender's numeric `id` alongside the login and `get_user_info()` returns `id` as well; comparing the immutable numeric ids would close both holes.

findings.title: User validation is skipped when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: The GitHub-user equality check only runs in the branch where an `Integration` row for the `installation_id` already exists. If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist` (line 481-482) the pipeline advances with no validation at all, so a caller who supplies someone else's `installation_id` can still bind that installation to their own Sentry org. This happens whenever the `installation` webhook has not been processed yet (race between the user finishing the pipeline and webhook delivery), was never delivered, or webhooks are not configured (self-hosted). A validation that does not depend on previously stored webhook data — e.g. calling `GET /user/installations` with the freshly obtained user access token and asserting the `installation_id` is listed — would cover this branch too.

findings.title: OAuth `state` is the pipeline signature, not a per-session nonce
findings.body: `state` is set to `pipeline.signature` and later compared against `request.GET["state"]`. The pipeline signature is derived from the pipeline's view set, so it is a constant value shared by every user and every organization — the tests hard-code it (`state=9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). A constant, publicly discoverable `state` provides no CSRF / authorization-code-injection protection for the OAuth callback: an attacker can always craft a callback URL with the correct `state`. The PR description lists this as one of the security checks, which overstates what it provides. Generate a random nonce per pipeline run, store it with `pipeline.bind_state(...)`, and compare that instead.

findings.title: Unhandled exception from get_user_info on GitHub API failure
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (from `sentry.identity.github`) performs a `GET /user` and raises on a non-2xx response rather than returning a payload. Unlike the surrounding code paths (bad state, missing access token), this call is not wrapped in try/except, so a transient GitHub 5xx, rate limit, or revoked token turns the install flow into an unhandled 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." page. Wrap the call and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` (ideally with logging/metrics so these failures are observable).

findings.title: Hard-coded redirect_uri must be registered as the GitHub App callback URL
findings.body: The authorize redirect sends `redirect_uri=<absolute_uri>/extensions/github/setup/`. GitHub rejects an authorize request whose `redirect_uri` is not under the callback URL registered for the app ("The redirect_uri MUST match the registered callback URL for this application"). Instances whose GitHub App/OAuth App is configured with a different callback URL (self-hosted setups are documented to point the user-authorization callback elsewhere, and single-tenant deployments use custom apps) will fail at the very first step of the integration install after this change. The PR contains no documentation or setup-instruction update for the newly required callback URL.

findings.title: Re-install now blocked for non-ACTIVE integrations
findings.body: After the `installations_exist` check, the code re-fetches the integration with `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` and renders the generic error if it is missing. Previously this branch (Integration row exists, no OrganizationIntegration) simply advanced the pipeline, so an Integration left in `PENDING_DELETION`/`DISABLED` with its org integrations already removed could be re-installed. Now such users get "We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request", which does not describe the real cause and gives them no actionable path. Either reuse the row already fetched on line 478 or report a status-specific message.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer covers the 404 path
findings.body: The test passes `state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05`, which differs from the valid pipeline signature used by every other test in this file (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`). The request therefore short-circuits in `OAuthLoginView` on the state-mismatch branch and the assertion `b"Invalid installation request."` passes for that reason alone. The behaviour the test is named for — `get_installation_info` returning 404 and `build_integration` raising `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")`, previously asserted — is now completely uncovered, and the 404 `responses.replace` setup is dead. Either use the correct state so the flow reaches `build_integration`, or rename the test to reflect that it only exercises state mismatch and add a separate test for the 404 case.

findings.title: No coverage for token-exchange failure branches
findings.body: The PR introduces two new failure branches in `OAuthLoginView` — the access-token exchange returning a body without `access_token` (wrong or reused `code`) and `get_user_info` returning a payload without `login` — and both are listed as intended failure modes in the description, but no test stubs a failing `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` or `/user` response. Regressions in these paths (e.g. an exception leaking a 500 instead of the error page) would go unnoticed.

findings.title: error_short strings are not extractable for translation
findings.body: `error()` takes `error_short` as a plain string and calls `_(error_short)` at runtime (line 141). Because the argument is a variable, `makemessages` cannot extract the literals ("Invalid installation request.", "GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization."), so these user-facing strings will never be translated even though the code implies they are. Mark the literals with `_()` at their definition/call sites and pass the already-lazy objects through.
